gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the eufy E340 runs on existing 16–24 V, 10 VA doorbell wiring but does not work with a digital chime, or that the SwitchBot kit's optional doorbell-to-monitor wire takes 5–6 V, 0.2 A DC and carries power only, with the monitor plugged into a 110–220 V AC outlet.
standout_why: I compared against the cited smarthomeperfected.com page, the cited eufy E10 and E340 bundle pages, worthrated.com, reolink.com/blog and drunvalo.net. Smart Home Perfected gives only 'Power: battery or wired' for the E340, says the SwitchBot monitor 'needs a power cable', and gives no voltage or chime limits. drunvalo.net says the E340 used 'the existing doorbell wiring' and 'Works with Eufy Smart Display E10', but it gives no voltage, nothing on digital chimes and no list of compatible doorbells. The eufy E10 product page asks 'Which eufy devices work with the Smart Display E10?' but gives no answer on the page. Worthrated and Reolink do not cover eufy or SwitchBot at all.
decides: This splits the pick by what the shopper already has at the door. If the house has a doorbell transformer and a mechanical chime, the eufy E340 + E10 can use that wiring and keep the old chime ringing. If the chime is digital, eufy's spec page says the E340 can't use it. eufy says its 'Use Provided Chime' option works, up to 4 chimes, but doesn't name a model. The SwitchBot kit is built around its own monitor. Its doorbell runs on a 5,000 mAh battery or USB-C. The only wired option is a 5–6 V DC power run from the monitor, and SwitchBot says it carries no data. The monitor needs a 110–220 V AC outlet. Shoppers who already own an older eufy doorbell can add just the E10 ($249.99), since eufy's list marks 13 eufy doorbells compatible. The E10 does not show other brands' cameras.
